title: Wandering off, then glancing back to check
summary: Most children move away and look to be sure you are still close by about 18 months, CDC says.
body: The child leaves the caregiver's side and then checks that the person is near. CDC treats that glance-back as a social milestone of this age. A laboratory separation procedure, with its named attachment patterns, is a different kind of description and is not what this line measures. Most means 75 percent or more on this series, and the sheet is not a diagnosis.

sources.title: Milestones by 18 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US government public domain. Supports 'Moves away from you, but looks to make sure you are close by'.
